speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the chronic, non-healing nature of these crusty lesions on sun-exposed areas and your history in a high-UV environment, Squamous Cell Carcinoma remains the primary concern. I will proceed with requesting a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy Findings: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. STD Panel: Syphilis Negative, HIV Negative, HBV Negative, HCV Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy findings of nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures are highly suggestive of a viral etiology, specifically Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection, which can present as chronic, non-healing lesions. Given your history in Africa and the specific histological features, I am considering a diagnosis of Erythema Ab Igne or a variant of HPV-related carcinoma, but the viral cytopathic effects point strongly toward HPV. DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma associated with High-Risk HPV
